hook: A May 2022 Air Force MISREP from the 196th Attack Squadron documenting an 18-hour-54-minute reconnaissance sortie over Iraq under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE, during which an ISR asset at 18,000 ft observed a single UAP flying north to northeast at 2043Z that the screener could not positively identify.
why_it_matters: This document demonstrates that by mid-2022, UAP reporting had been formally integrated into standard military operational reporting formats — the MISREP includes a dedicated UAP section with standardized fields (contact DTG, asset location, trajectory, observer effects) submitted directly to AARO. The UAP encounter itself is minimally described: the observer followed the object as long as possible, all key parameters (altitude, velocity, type) are listed as unknown, and the screener could not obtain a positive ID, illustrating the limits of available ISR collection against the observed object. The SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY classification indicates the report was shared across Five Eyes partners.
key_findings: A single UAP was observed at 2043Z on May 20, 2022, flying north to northeast from grid 38SMC79[redacted]70[redacted]; the observing asset was at 18,000 ft and grid 38SMC85[redacted]77[redacted] at time of contact — all UAP parameters including altitude, velocity, and trajectory were recorded as unknown
The screener followed the UAP 'as long as possible' but could not obtain a positive identification; the UAP MDS type and tail number were both recorded as UNK

The 196th Attack Squadron flew an 18-hour-54-minute reconnaissance mission from OKAS (0542Z May 20 to 0036Z May 21), collecting SIGINT via AIRHANDLER Version 2 for approximately 21 hours while supporting Operation PHANTOM FLEX

FMV (Full Motion Video) was collected and exploited by DGS 1; the aircraft carried a TGT Pod (ANDAS4) and AIRHANDLER Version 2 avionics, operated under the 609th CAOC and Air Combat Command (ACC) within USCENTCOM
The ISR section supported a unit designated 'MAG' under a redacted operation name with 136 minutes of pre-coordination, assessed as satisfactory; the intel gap fill was confirmed as effective

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The MISREP was formally approved for release to AARO and uses AARO's standardized UAP reporting fields, placing it directly within the AARO reporting chain established after 2022.
The document carries SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY classification, indicating it was authorized for sharing with Five Eyes partners, extending UAP reporting visibility beyond U.S.-only channels.
